safi-cedvel:2-2.t:
* I'rab:
(قد) a particle of realisation (ḥarf taḥqīq); (لكم) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (فرض), in the sense of "prescribed"; (الواو) resumptive — or circumstantial (ḥāliyya) — and the second one is a conjunction.
The clause «قد فرض اللَّه ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «اللَّه مولاكم ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive [Note: It may be in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).].
The clause «هو العليم ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause اللَّه مولاكم.

* Morphology:
(تحلّة): a maṣdar (verbal noun) known by hearing (samāʿī) of the quadriliteral حلّل; the regular (qiyāsī) one is تحليل.

safi-cedvel:3-3.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (إذ) an adverb of past time, in the position of accusative, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted verb indicated by His words العليم الخبير, i.e. "Allah knew"; (إلى بعض) attached to (أسرّ); (الفاء) conjunction; (لمّا) an adverb in the sense of "when", containing the meaning of condition, in the position of accusative, attached to the apodosis عرّف; (به) attached to (نبّأت); (عليه) attached to (أظهره) by its being made to carry (taḍmīn) the meaning of أطلعه "informed him"; (عن بعض) attached to (أعرض); (فلمّا نبّأها به) is like فلما نبّأت به.
The clause «أسرّ النبيّ ...» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «نبّات به ...» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «أظهره ...» is in the position of genitive, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause نبّأت به [Note: It may be parenthetical, or in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) with قد implied.].
The clause «عرّف ...» has no grammatical position: apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «أعرض ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the apodosis.
The clause «نبّأها به ...» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «قالت ...» has no grammatical position: apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «من أنبأك ...» is in the position of accusative as the object of speech (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «أنبأك هذا ...» is in the position of nominative as khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (من).
The clause «قال ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «نبّأني العليم ...» is in the position of accusative as the object of speech.

safi-cedvel:4-5.t:
* I'rab:
(إلى اللَّه) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (تتوبا); (الفاء) causal (taʿlīliyya); (قد) a particle of realisation (ḥarf taḥqīq); (الواو) conjunction; (تظاهرا) an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), from which one of the two tāʾs has been deleted; (عليه) attached to (تظاهرا); (الفاء) causal; (هو) a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl) [Note: Or a detached pronoun in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), whose khabar (predicate) is مولاه, the nominal clause being the khabar of إنّ.]; (جبريل) a mubtadaʾ, nominative (marfūʿ), whose khabar is (ظهير) [Note: Or it is conjoined to the position of إنّ and its noun — whose position is nominative — and (الملائكة) is then a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is ظهير, the clause being independent of the first and conjoined to it.]; (صالح) conjoined (maʿṭūf) to جبريل, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the wāw, which has been deleted for lightness, in keeping with the reading in continuous recitation (waṣl); (بعد) an accusative adverb, attached to the khabar ظهير.
The clause «تتوبا ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive. The apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, its implied form being "He will accept from you both" or "you will both be accepted".
The clause «قد صغت قلوبكما ...» has no grammatical position: a causal explanation of the condition, i.e.: if you both repent to Allah — because you have both inclined with your own selves — He will accept repentance from you both.
The clause «تظاهرا ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause تتوبا. The apodosis is omitted, its implied form being "he will find a helper who helps him".
The clause «إن اللَّه ... مولاه» has no grammatical position: a causal explanation of the second apodosis.
The clause «جبريل ... ظهير» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the last causal clause.
5- (طلّقكنّ) a past verb in the position of jussive as protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); (أن) an infinitival and subjunctive-governing particle; (خيرا) a naʿt (adjective) of (أزواجا), accusative (manṣūb); (منكنّ) attached to (خيرا); (مسلمات ...) ḥāl (circumstantial) of (أزواجا) [Note: It has become specified by the naʿt. It may also be a second naʿt of (أزواجا), along with the rest of the other descriptions.], accusative.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يبدله ...) is in the position of accusative as khabar of عسى.
The clause «عسى ربّه ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «طلّقكنّ ...» has no grammatical position: parenthetical. The apodosis is omitted, indicated by what precedes, i.e.: if he divorces you, then perhaps his Lord will give him in exchange...
The clause «يبدله ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila (relative clause) of the particle relative (أن).

* Morphology:
(صغت): it contains iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by deletion on account of the meeting of two quiescent letters; the lām of the word has been deleted. Its pattern is فعت.
(ثيّبات): plural of ثيّب, a feminine generic noun (ism jins); the woman is so called because she returns (تثوب) to her parents' house. Its pattern is فيعل, and it contains iʿlāl by substitution: its original form is ثيوب — with sukūn on the yāʾ and kasra on the wāw — the wāw was changed into yāʾ and assimilated into the other yāʾ.

* Rhetoric:
The secret of the plural: in His words «قلوبكما».
The plural is used in «قلوبكما» rather than the dual, because of the dislike of two duals coming together, while the intended meaning is clear; in such cases this is more commonly used than the dual or the singular.

safi-cedvel:6-6.t:
* I'rab:
(يأيّها الذين) is like يأيّها النبيّ [Note: In verse (1) of Sūrat al-Ṭalāq.]; (نارا) a second mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative, governed by (قوا); (عليها) attached to (mutaʿalliq) a fronted khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (ملائكة); (لا) negative; (ما) an infinitival particle [Note: Or a relative noun in the position of genitive by an omitted preposition, with the referent pronoun omitted, i.e.: in what He commanded them.], and the second one is a relative, with the referent pronoun omitted.
The interpreted maṣdar (ما أمرهم ...) is in the position of accusative as a badal (substitute) of the Name of Majesty, i.e.: they do not disobey Allah's command.
The clause «النداء ...» (the vocative) has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «آمنوا ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذين).
The clause «قوا ...» has no grammatical position: response to the vocative.
The clause «وقودها الناس» is in the position of accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of (نارا).
The clause «عليها ملائكة ...» is in the position of accusative as a second naʿt of (نارا).
The clause «لا يعصون ...» is in the position of nominative as a naʿt of ملائكة.
The clause «يفعلون ...» is in the position of nominative, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause لا يعصون.
The clause «أمرهم ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila of the particle relative (ما).
The clause «يؤمرون» has no grammatical position: ṣila of the relative (ما).

* Morphology:
(قوا): it contains iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by deletion in two places. The first is the fāʾ of the word, beginning from the imperfect because it fell between a yāʾ and a kasra; the deletion then extended to the imperative — as in the mithāl weak verb. The second is the lām of the word, also beginning from the imperfect, where it was attributed to the wāw of the plural; then the deletion extended to the imperative. The original form is يقيونا: the ḍamma was felt heavy on the yāʾ, so it was made quiescent and the vowel was transferred to the qāf [Note: Some said: the yāʾ was deleted because of its heaviness, then the qāf was given ḍamma to suit the wāw.]; when two quiescent letters met, the yāʾ was deleted; then the deletion carried over to the imperative, and the nūn was deleted for indeclinability (bināʾ). Its pattern is عوا.
(يعصون): it contains iʿlāl by deletion; its original form is يعصيون: the ḍamma was felt heavy on the yāʾ, so it was made quiescent and the vowel was transferred to the ṣād; when two quiescent letters met, the yāʾ was deleted, and it became يعصون. Its pattern is يفعون.

* Rhetoric:
The device of negation and affirmation (al-salb wa-l-ījāb): in His words لا يَعْصُونَ اللَّهَ ما أَمَرَهُمْ وَيَفْعَلُونَ ما يُؤْمَرُونَ.
This device is building speech upon negating a thing from one aspect and affirming it from another, or commanding a thing from one aspect and forbidding it from other than that aspect.
In the noble verse, He, Mighty and Majestic, negated disobedience of those so described, and affirmed obedience for them.

safi-cedvel:7-7.t:
* I'rab:
(لا) a prohibitive, jussive-governing particle; (اليوم) an adverb of time, accusative, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (تعتذروا); (إنّما) the restraining particle and the restrained (kāffa wa-makfūfa); (الواو) in (تجزون) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); (ما) an infinitival particle [Note: Or a relative noun in the position of accusative, with the referent pronoun omitted.].
The interpreted maṣdar (ما كنتم ...) is in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object) with a muḍāf omitted, i.e.: the recompense of what you used to...
The clause «النداء ...» (the vocative) has no grammatical position: resumptive [Note: Or it is in the position of accusative as the object of speech (maqūl al-qawl) of an implied saying, i.e.: the angels say ...].
The clause «كفروا ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذين).
The clause «لا تعتذروا ...» has no grammatical position: response to the vocative.
The clause «تجزون ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «كنتم تعملون ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila of the particle relative (ما).
The clause «تعملون» is in the position of accusative as khabar (predicate) of كنتم.

safi-cedvel:8-8.t:
* I'rab:
(إلى اللَّه) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (توبوا); (أن) an infinitival and subjunctive-governing particle; (عنكم) attached to (يكفّر) by its being made to carry (taḍmīn) the meaning of ينزل "remove"; (الواو) conjunction in the four places; (يدخلكم) an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb), conjoined (maʿṭūf) to (يكفّر); (من تحتها) attached to (تجري) with a muḍāf omitted, i.e. from beneath its trees [Note: Or attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) of الأنهار.]; (يوم) an adverb of time, accusative, attached to (يدخلكم) [Note: Or it is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb, its implied form being "remember".]; (لا) negative; (الذين) a relative in the position of accusative, conjoined to النبيّ [Note: Or in the position of nominative, whose khabar is the clause نورهم يسعى ...]; (معه) an accusative adverb, attached to (آمنوا); (بين) an accusative adverb, attached to (يسعى) [Note: Or attached to a ḥāl of the fāʿil of يسعى.]; (بأيمانهم) attached to what بين is attached to, for it is conjoined to it; (لنا) attached to (أتمم), and the second one attached to (اغفر); (على كلّ) attached to the khabar (predicate) (قدير).
The clause «النداء ...» (the vocative) has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «آمنوا ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذين).
The clause «توبوا ...» has no grammatical position: response to the vocative.
The clause «عسى ربّكم ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «يكفّر ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila of the particle relative (أن).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يكفّر ...) is in the position of accusative as khabar of عسى.
The clause «يدخلكم ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause يكفّر.
The clause «تجري ...» is in the position of accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of جنّات.
The clause «لا يخزي اللَّه ...» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «آمنوا» (the second) has no grammatical position: ṣila of the second relative (الذين).
The clause «نورهم يسعى ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive [Note: Or it is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl of النبيّ and الذين آمنوا معه.].
The clause «يسعى ...» is in the position of nominative as khabar of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (نورهم).
The clause «يقولون ...» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl of the pronoun in أيديهم [Note: Or it is resumptive, with no grammatical position.].
The clause «النداء ...» (the vocative) is in the position of accusative as the object of speech (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «أتمم ...» has no grammatical position: response to the vocative.
The clause «اغفر لنا ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the response to the vocative.
The clause «إنّك ... قدير» has no grammatical position: causal (taʿlīliyya).

* Morphology:
(نصوحا): a ṣifa mushabbaha (assimilated adjective) from the triliteral نصح ... or it is one of the intensive forms (ṣiyagh al-mubālagha). Its pattern is فعول with fatḥa on the fāʾ.

* Rhetoric:
Figurative attribution (al-isnād al-majāzī): in His words تَوْبَةً نَصُوحاً.
Repentance has been described as sincere (nuṣḥ) by way of figurative attribution, whereas sincerity is the attribute of those who repent: that they counsel themselves sincerely with repentance, and so perform it in its proper way, making amends for past failings and erasing evil deeds.

safi-cedvel:9-9.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) a conjunction in the three places, and circumstantial (ḥāliyya) — or resumptive — in the fourth place. The one specified for blame (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-dhamm) is omitted, its implied form being "هي", i.e. Hell.
The clause «النداء ...» (the vocative) has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «جاهد ...» has no grammatical position: response to the vocative.
The clause «اغلظ ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the response to the vocative.
The clause «مأواهم جهنّم» has no grammatical position: conjoined to an implied causal clause, i.e.: We shall call them to account, and their refuge is Hell ...
The clause «بئس المصير» has no grammatical position: resumptive [Note: Or a ḥāl (circumstantial) of جهنّم, the governing factor in it being ibtidāʾ (inception as subject).].

safi-cedvel:10-12.t:
* I'rab:
(مثلا) a second mafʿūl bihi (direct object), fronted; (للذين) attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of (مثلا) [Note: Or attached to (مثلا).]; (امرأة) a first mafʿūl bihi, postponed [Note: With a muḍāf omitted, i.e. the state of the wife.], accusative; (الواو) conjunction in both places; (تحت) an accusative adverb, attached to the khabar (predicate) of كانتا, the adverbial sense being figurative; (من عبادنا) attached to a naʿt of (عبدين); (الفاء) conjunction in both places; (عنهما) attached to (يغنيا) by its being made to carry (taḍmīn) the meaning of يدفعا "ward off"; (من الله) attached to (يغنيا) with a muḍāf omitted, i.e. from the punishment of Allah; (شيئا) a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for the maṣdar [Note: Or it is an accusative mafʿūl bihi.], i.e. anything of avail; (مع) an accusative adverb, attached to (ادخلا).
The clause «ضرب الله ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «كفروا ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذين).
The clause «كانتا تحت ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «خانتاهما ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause كانتا ...
The clause «لم يغنيا ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause خانتاهما.
The clause «قيل ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause لم يغنيا.
The clause «ادخلا ...» is in the position of nominative as nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) [Note: Because it is the object of speech (maqūl al-qawl) with the active verb.].
11- (الواو) conjunction in the four places; (ضرب الله ... امرأة فرعون) is like ضرب الله ... امرأة نوح; (إذ) an adverb of past time, in the position of accusative, attached to (مثلا); (ربّ) one addressed in the vocative (munādā), a muḍāf, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the fatḥa implied (muqaddar) on the letter before the yāʾ of the first person, which has been deleted for lightness; (لي) attached to (ابن); (عندك) an accusative adverb, attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun in (لي) [Note: Or to a ḥāl of (بيتا), being a naʿt placed before what it qualifies ... And (في الجنّة) may be a badal (substitute) — or ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) — of the adverb عندك ...]; (في الجنّة) attached to a naʿt of (بيتا); (من فرعون) attached to (نجّني); (من القوم) attached to the second (نجّني) ...
The clause «ضرب الله» (the second) has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause ضرب الله (the first).
The clause «آمنوا ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila of the second relative (الذين).
The clause «قالت ...» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «النداء وجوابه ...» (the vocative and its response) is in the position of accusative as the object of speech.
The clause «ابن لي ...» has no grammatical position: response to the vocative.
The clause «نجّني» (the first) ... has no grammatical position: conjoined to the response to the vocative.
The clause «نجّني» (the second) ... has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause نجّني (the first).
12- (الواو) conjunction in the four places; (مريم) conjoined to (امرأة فرعون), accusative; (بنة) a badal of مريم — or ʿaṭf bayān to it — accusative; (التي) a relative in the position of accusative as a naʿt of مريم; (فيه) attached to (نفخنا), the pronoun referring to her chastity (farj) figuratively, because the breathing was into the opening of her garment; (من روحنا) attached to (نفخنا), and (من) is partitive; (بكلمات) attached to (صدّقت); (من القانتين) attached to the khabar of كانت ...
The clause «أحصنت ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila of the relative (التي).
The clause «نفخنا ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the ṣila clause.
The clause «صدّقت ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to an implied resumptive clause, i.e.: so she conceived ʿĪsā and believed in the words ...
The clause «كانت من القانتين ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause صدّقت [Note: The clause may be a ḥāl with قد implied.] ...

* Rhetoric:
1- Representation (al-tamthīl): in His words «ضَرَبَ اللَّهُ مَثَلًا ...» — the verse.
Allah, Mighty and Majestic, likened the state of the disbelievers — in that they are punished for their disbelief and their enmity towards the believers with a punishment like theirs, without leniency or favouritism, and that whatever bond of kinship by lineage or tie by marriage there was between them and the believers does not benefit them alongside their enmity, because their enmity towards him and their disbelief in Allah and His Messenger cut the ties and severed the connection, and made them further than strangers, and further still, even if the believer to whom the disbeliever is connected is a prophet among the prophets of Allah — to the state of the wife of Nūḥ and the wife of Lūṭ: when they acted hypocritically and betrayed the two messengers, the two messengers did not avail them at all against the punishment of Allah, by right of the marriage bond between them.
2- Allusion (al-taʿrīḍ): in His words «ضَرَبَ اللَّهُ مَثَلًا» — the verse. In the striking of these two similitudes there is an allusion to the two Mothers of the Believers mentioned at the beginning of the sūra and to what they had committed of backing each other against the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in what he disliked, and a warning to them in the sternest and strongest way, because of the mention of disbelief in the similitude; and an indication that it was their due to be, in sincerity and in perfection in it, like these two believing women, and not to rely on their being wives of the Messenger of Allah. The allusion to Ḥafṣa is more likely, because the wife of Lūṭ disclosed his secret just as Ḥafṣa disclosed the secret of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.

* Benefits:
The purity of the honour of the prophets ...
In this verse Allah struck a similitude: that the corrupt, disobedient disbeliever is not benefited by the righteousness of another, even if he were a prophet. The wife of Nūḥ, whose name was Wāʿila — and it was said: Wālʿa — and the wife of Lūṭ, whose name was Wāhila — and it was said: Wālha — were wives of two righteous servants who were prophets, namely Nūḥ and Lūṭ, upon them be blessings and peace (فخانتاهما). Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: The wife of a prophet never committed fornication; their betrayal was only that they were upon a religion other than theirs. The wife of Nūḥ used to say to people: He is mad, and when anyone believed in him she would inform the tyrants of her people. As for the wife of Lūṭ, she used to direct her people to his guests: when a guest came to him at night she would light a fire, and when a guest came to him by day she would make smoke, to let her people know of that. Therefore the scholars are unanimous on the purity of the honour of the prophets, and they said: if the wife of a prophet persists in disbelief, this does not impugn his honour and his protection (ʿiṣma); but if she were to commit fornication, this would not accord with the protection of the prophets and their purity, for their honour is safeguarded from fornication, and so that never occurs among their women.

safi-cedvel:1-1.t:
* I'rab:
(يا أيّها النبيّ) its i'rab has already been given [Note: in verse (1) of Sūrat al-Ṭalāq]. (لم) attached to (تحرّم); and (ما) is an interrogative noun from which the alif has been deleted. (ما) a relative [Note: or a specified indefinite] in the position of accusative, a direct object. (لك) attached to (أحلّ). (الواو) resumptive – or circumstantial (ḥāliyya).
Clause: «النداء ... » (the vocative) has no grammatical position; it is an initial clause.
And the clause: «تحرّم ... » has no grammatical position; it is the response to the vocative.
And the clause: «أحلّ اللَّه ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative (ما) [Note: or it is in the position of accusative, an adjective of (ما)].
And the clause: «تبتغي ... » is in the position of accusative, a ḥāl from the fāʿil of تحرّم.
And the clause: «اللَّه غفور ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive [Note: It is permissible that it be in the position of accusative as a ḥāl].

* Benefits:
1- (يا أَيُّهَا) The one addressed (munādā): an overt noun mentioned after one of the particles of vocation, to request the attention of its referent or alert him, such as: (يا خالد اذهب إلى الملعب) ("O Khālid, go to the playground").
The particles of vocation are: (يا، أيا، هيا، أي، والهمزة).
Their specialisation: (أي and the hamza) are for calling one who is near; (أيا and هيا) for calling one who is far; and (يا) for every one addressed.
Kinds of the one addressed: First: indeclinable on whatever it would be raised with, in the position of accusative; and it is of two types: (a) when it is a singular proper name, i.e. neither a muḍāf nor resembling a muḍāf, such as: (يُوسُفُ أَعْرِضْ عَنْ هذا). (b) When it is a specified indefinite, which is the particular indefinite, as when we say to someone in front of us: (يا رجل أقبل).
Second: accusative with fatḥa or what stands in for it, and it is of three types:
1- the muḍāf addressed, such as: يا عبد اللَّه; 2- the addressed resembling a muḍāf, such as: يا حافظا وقته أبشر بالفوز; 3- the unspecified indefinite addressed, such as: يا جنديا احترس. The one addressed in these three types is declinable (muʿrab), and the accusative is obligatory.
2- The scholars differed regarding the expression of prohibition (taḥrīm). It was said that it is not an oath. If a man says to his wife: "You are forbidden to me" or says "I have made you forbidden", then if he intended divorce it is a divorce; if he intended ẓihār, it is ẓihār; and if he intended to forbid her person or spoke without specifying, he owes the expiation of an oath. If he says that to his slave girl, then if he intended emancipation, he has freed her; and if he intended to forbid her person or spoke without specifying, he owes the expiation of an oath. If he says of food: "I have forbidden it to myself", nothing is due from him. This is the opinion of Abū Bakr, ʿUmar, a group of the Companions and Successors, and al-Shāfiʿī.
